items.title: CAS-wiring-adjacent language rung: citable boolean-comparison formulas
items.notes: Discovered while scoping wave2-k2-math-cardinality-comparison: ADJ had no way to express a citable, queryable, parameterized 'is A greater than B' — `formula` bodies were arithmetic-only, and `constrain`/`check` (the language's only comparison surface) carries no provenance tail and isn't `?`-queryable. Researched the AST/evaluator/formula_audit.rs blast radius first (compiler-enforced exhaustive matches; confirmed the CAS-provenance agent's adj_stdlib_provenance.py verify only touches its own registered manifest, so an unmigrated comparison formula fails closed, never crashes CI) before implementing. Adds `formula_relation = expr [ relop expr ]` (grammar-additive, every existing formula still parses), `ExprAst::Compare`, 6 new `ComputeOp::Cmp*` variants (dimensionless 1/0 result, exact when operands are, mirrors `Sign`'s dimension-collapse). Spec'd in ADJ-FORMULA-LIBRARIES.md §3B (FL-8). Full test coverage (logic-engine + adj-lang unit/e2e + formula_source_map), clippy clean. Ships as its own PR ahead of the K-2 content PR that will actually use it (comparison.adj).

items.title: K-2 math: cardinality/sets, comparison, number lines
items.notes: New content per ADJ-STDLIB-COVERAGE.md 5.1. Checked adj-ladder rung0 for harvestable material - none (rung0_arithmetic is generic MCQ word-problem benchmark items, not cardinality/comparison/number-line pedagogical content). Shipped 3 library pairs in code/specs/data/adj-formula-stdlib/mathematics/: number-sequence.adj (next/previous, composes arithmetic.adj's sum/difference, K.CC.A.1/A.2), comparison.adj (greater_than via FL-8, K.CC.C.6/C.7), cardinality.adj (total_cardinality composing sum, K.CC.B.4/B.5). All 3 citations WebFetch-verified live against MathWorld before writing (CountingNumber/Greater/CardinalNumber pages). Added 3 manifest.json objectives (adj.math.k2.*, band K-2, mathematics, ccss.math). Added a dedicated e2e test file (code/packages/rust/adj-lang-cli/tests/formula_k2_math_e2e.rs, 5 tests) actually executing each query file, not just structural checks. Also added the long-missing README.md/CHANGELOG.md at adj-formula-stdlib/ package root (flagged as a gap during Wave 0).

items.title: Elementary math: base-ten place value and word-problem schemas
items.notes: Next Wave 2 K-8 gap per ADJ-STDLIB-COVERAGE.md 5.1's elementary row: 'base-ten procedures, word-problem schemas' are named Major Gaps with nothing shipped yet (unlike fractions/decimals/percent, which arithmetic/ already covers: fraction.adj, percent.adj, average.adj). Shipped mathematics/place-value.adj: tens_and_ones_to_number(tens, ones) = sum(product(tens, 10), ones), composing arithmetic.adj (CCSS 1.NBT.B.2), cited to mathsisfun.com's positional-notation definition (trust consensus), WebFetch-verified live before writing. Scoped as COMPOSE-direction only (digits -> number); DECOMPOSE (number -> digits) needs floor/modulo division, not reachable from the plain-arithmetic surface grammar today (only `latex "..."` reaches ComputeOp::Floor/Mod) - see the new wave2-place-value-decompose item this discovered. Added manifest objective adj.math.k2.place_value and a dedicated e2e test (formula_place_value_e2e.rs, 2 tests, both executed against the real CLI).

items.title: Wire floor/mod into the plain-arithmetic surface grammar to unblock place-value decomposition
items.notes: Confirmed the hypothesis: floor/mod needed NO grammar change, just two new recognized-by-name built-ins in lower.rs's expand_rec (RUNTIME_BUILTIN_FORMULAS), mapping directly onto the pre-existing ExprAst::Floor/ExprAst::Bin(ArithOp::Mod,..) nodes -- zero new exhaustive-match sites, much smaller than FL-8. Spec'd in ADJ-FORMULA-LIBRARIES.md 3C (FL-9). Extended mathematics/place-value.adj with tens_digit(n)=floor(n/10) and ones_digit(n)=mod(n,10), verified as algebraic inverses of the existing tens_and_ones_to_number (round-trip e2e test). No new manifest objective needed (same adj.math.k2.place_value objective/library file). Full test coverage (adj-lang unit/e2e including arity-error and reserved-name anti-drift tests, adj-lang-cli e2e), clippy clean. adj-lang bumped 0.72.0->0.73.0; adj-lang-cli NOT bumped (test-only addition, matching this repo's convention of only bumping on actual source changes).

items.title: CAS-wiring rung-0 (ADJ-FORMULA-LIBRARIES 3D, FL-10): `symbolic ... for <var>`, bind-then-solve a single linear equation via symbolic-vm::Backend + cas-solve
items.notes: User explicitly authorized adj-lang language changes ('if the language is lacking features that makes this kind of work difficult, add support to it') and confirmed proceeding autonomously ('you can make most of the decisions yourself... it's reversible'). Design researched via Explore + direct source reading before implementing: cas-solve has no public 'solve a plain linear equation, leaving other variables free' entry point (only solve_linear(a,b)/solve_linear_system(equations,variables), both requiring every non-target identifier already reduced to a number) -- so rung-0 is deliberately bind-then-solve (every parameter except the one named after `for` must already be observed). Mid-implementation the user corrected the initial design (which called cas_solve::solve_linear directly as a free function) with 'the CAS packages are not designed to be used directly, they are designed to be used through the Symbolic VM' -- confirmed via AskUserQuestion, then REDESIGNED to route through a new minimal symbolic_vm::Backend (crate::symbolic_backend::RungZeroBackend in adj-lang), mirroring macsyma-runtime's MacsymaBackend/solve_handler (the one existing example of this Backend/VM pattern in the repo), dispatching to cas_solve::solve_linear_system via symbolic_vm::VM::eval. Ships `physics/electricity.adj`'s Ohm's law both directions (existing forward `formula voltage(...)` + new `symbolic resistance_from_ohms_law(...) for resistance`). Also fixed a real pre-existing-shape bug the worked example surfaced: enforce_vocabulary's check_query only special-cased the `formulas` registry, so a `symbolic` application in any `use`/`dictionary`-scoped program was rejected as UndefinedTerm despite lowering correctly. Pre-push security review (2 rounds) found and fixed one MEDIUM: exact_rational_to_irnode's i64 narrowing accepted the i64::MIN boundary, which Frac::new/symbolic_ir::rat then negate with unchecked i64 arithmetic (overflow) -- fixed with a checked_i64 helper at both narrowing sites, regression test added, second review round clean. 14 new adj-lang unit tests + full existing suite green (247 lib tests total), clippy clean, adj_stdlib_report.py/adj_stdlib_manifest.py both exit 0. PR #10015 pushed with gh pr merge --auto --squash set; awaiting CI. NEXT (not started): free (unbound) non-target variables, quadratic+/transcendental solving, and a real symbolic-identity provenance shape (StepKind::FromRewrite, currently reuses the plain formula DerivationNode::Op shape as an accepted rung-0 limitation) are all explicitly out of scope for rung-0 and are candidate rung-1 items if the user wants to keep going on CAS-wiring rather than return to Wave-2/3/4 content.
